suggestions.rationale: Degenerative changes or bulging discs in the lumbar spine frequently compress the sciatic nerve roots, causing radiating pain, numbness, or tingling down the leg (sciatica).
evidenceGaps: EMG/NCS test results showing nerve impingement
Medical nexus connecting nerve compression to the service-connected lumbar condition

sourceReferences.note: Authorizes secondary connection for disabilities proximately caused by a service-connected condition.

sourceReferences.citation: VA M21-1, Part V, Subpart iii, Chapter 1, Section B
sourceReferences.note: Guidelines on evaluating peripheral nerve conditions secondary to spinal disorders.

suggestions.rationale: Compression of the upper lumbar nerve roots (L2-L4) can cause femoral nerve radiculopathy, resulting in anterior thigh pain and weakness.
evidenceGaps: Imaging (MRI) showing upper lumbar nerve root compression

suggestions.rationale: Chronic, severe lower back pain and resulting functional limitations can lead to the development of secondary depression.
evidenceGaps: Treatment records showing pain interfering with sleep and daily activities
Nexus opinion linking depression specifically to chronic pain from the back condition
